outcome: The book is grasped and carried to the caddy but is released/dropped in the front compartment (EEF y ≈ -0.15) instead of the back compartment (y ≈ -0.24 to -0.30); the episode runs to the step budget with the task incomplete.
immediate_trigger: At step ~430-450 the gripper gap collapses to ~0.001 (fingers close on empty) while the EEF is still stalled at y ≈ -0.15, releasing the book in the front compartment rather than the back compartment.
root_cause: The frozen Pi0.5 full-task VLA policy undershoots the placement target: its learned trajectory stops the EEF at the caddy front compartment (y ≈ -0.15) and stalls there (stalled=1, direction cosine oscillating around 0), never advancing to the back-compartment depth (y ≈ -0.24 to -0.30) that the success comparator reaches. The book is consequently released in the wrong compartment. This is a VLA policy undershoot, not a scripted-servo singularity (no move_to/IK was ever called).
contributing_causes: The VLA replans every 5 steps and, once stalled at the front compartment, emits oscillatory near-zero-progress commands (direction cosine hovering around 0) that consume the remaining step budget without advancing depth.

Grasp retention is marginal (grip gap ~0.029 near the closed threshold); in one failure (bc9c69b9) the grip drifts open to ~0.059, indicating the book can slip during the stall, converting an undershoot into a guaranteed drop.
competing_hypotheses: Root cause: VLA placement undershoot — the policy stops at the front compartment (y ≈ -0.15) and stalls, releasing the book short of the back compartment.
Alternative: grasp-retention failure — the book slips out of a marginal grasp during the carry, and the EEF 'stall' is the policy reacting to the lost grasp rather than a placement-target error.
affected_component: frozen Pi0.5 full-task VLA policy (placement phase)
earliest_divergence: Step ~170-190: in the success episode the EEF continues advancing to y ≈ -0.24 with the gripper locked at 0.029, while in all three failures the EEF stops at y ≈ -0.15 and begins stalling (stalled=1, direction cosine dropping toward 0).
falsifier: If, in a failure episode, the gripper gap had collapsed to ~0.001 (book released) while the EEF was still advancing toward y ≈ -0.24, the placement-undershoot hypothesis would be refuted in favor of grasp-retention failure. Conversely, if the book were held (gap ~0.029) through the entire stall and only released at the front compartment, grasp-retention is excluded for that episode.
distinguishing_check: Compare, at the same array position, the gripper gap at the moment the EEF first stalls (stalled=1) versus when the gap collapses to ~0.001: in failures 1 and 3 the gap stays at book-thickness (0.029-0.036) through step ~430 while the EEF is stalled at y ≈ -0.15, only collapsing at step ~440 — meaning the book was HELD during the stall, so the stall precedes and causes the drop (placement undershoot). Failure 2 (bc9c69b9) instead shows the gap drifting open to ~0.059 by step 410, consistent with an early slip — evidence of within-cluster heterogeneity. A paired live run with a longer placement horizon / explicit back-compartment prompt versus the frozen policy would directly test whether the undershoot is a policy-depth error.
required_validation: paired live experiment needed before acceptance
